_what_this_is: the 2026-09-12 relocation of loose `logs/` material into the experiment that owns it. Every move is old path -> new path, so a citation in an older document can be followed forward. Nothing was copied and nothing was deleted.

reverted._why: these 24 were moved and MOVED BACK the same day. They are components the run index registers WITH A DIGEST, and a registered component is evidence at a path: moving it makes the recorded digest describe nothing. The first pass missed them because the index stores `components` (role -> path) and `component_digests` (role -> digest) as two separate maps, so a check looking for one object carrying both a path and a hash found neither.
reverted._also_reverted: 15 README files INSIDE registered directories, whose links the link-fixer had repointed. The digest covers the directory, so editing a file in it changes registered evidence. Their bytes were restored from git. A stale link inside frozen evidence is correct -- it records where things were when the evidence was written.
reverted._second_class: six of these were reverted for a different reason again: a registered directory's own text CITES them in prose -- a session record or a run README naming the grant it ran under. The citation carries no hash and no executable reads it, so neither the digest check nor the reference check saw it; what makes it binding is that the citing document cannot be corrected, because correcting it changes the digest that makes it evidence. The target holds still instead.
